title: The mountain hotel at Kanazawa and Japan as the trip's best part
summary: A hot-springs mountain hotel gave a sukiyaki dinner; Holmes liked Japan most, preferring not to be stationed in Tokyo like Herbie Cowens's group.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Then we had a little vacation. They sent us to a hotel in Kanizawa(?) where we spent, I don't know, about five or six days there -- a beautiful hotel on the side of a

mountain. It's a nine-mile slope, a nine-mile slope to the top of the mountain. When you get up there, then that's one story in the hotel. You go in the hotel, and you're walkin' down through the side of it. It was very unique. That was the most beautiful hotel. They had hot spring water in the place, bath water, a pool space, all through the hotel. Hot springs. Of course, when you take a bath, everybody gets in the bath together. That's what they told me. I have never seen that. You know, I've seen the baths, but I've never seen nobody else in the water. That was a beautiful hotel. Very (?).

And we stayed there. They gave us a big sukiyaki dinner, and it was beautiful. They had about fifty girls, Japanese girls working in the place. There was about eight or ten officers, American officers living in this big hotel. I don't know how many rooms it was. Some rooms in there they had never even looked in. But there was fifty girls as help in the place, to wait on those ten or twelve officers.

Well, they gave us a big dinner, and we were all sitting around on cushions and eating the sukiyāki, drinkin' that wine and stuff that they have. So when I go to bed... Bacon and I, we were roommates. And over there you sleep in a pallet on the floor. Next morning I woke up, Bacon laughed at me and said, "Well, that's the first time I seen
anybody fall off of a pallet before." I was so drunk, I just rolled off of the pallet.

But that was nice. A nice adventure(?). Japan was a beautiful place. Out of the whole trip, I liked Japan the most. Well, we were there for one month, and we was doing two and three days here, three and four days some other place. We made a lot of (?).

Now, Herbie Cowens, his group, they were in Japan at the same time we were. They were on the same boat. When we left Okinawa, they were on the same boat. But they hit Japan the same time we did, but they were stationed right in Japan, right in Tokyo -- they were stationed right in Tokyo. Now, I didn't like that, because I wanted to be stationed in Tokyo. I didn't want to be running around the country. But now I'm glad that I did. It gave me a chance to see Japan as it was. They stayed right there for the whole month. They didn't see nothin' but Tokyo. But other than that...
